title: 遊ぶ
grammarName: Sentence particles: ね / よ + ている progressive
grammarPatterns: Xが変わる (state change, bridging to ch12)
plotSummary: A summer afternoon in the Moomin garden. Everyone is playing hide-and-seek — Moomintroll is the oni, the others hide. Sniff's eyes glint behind the tree; Ninny is only a stirring in the grass. The sentence-final particles ね and よ take their staircase home here — and the ている-progressive describes what each child is doing right now ("hiding", "looking", "running").

scene.location: ムーミンやしきとにわ
scene.beat: Playing. The children run and stop and run. The eyes look for each other; the pace turns from labeling to moving. Little My's voice is loud at the edges.

prose.text: いい天気の午後、ムーミンの庭で、みんなが遊んでいた。

grammarNotes: 〜ね — an agreement / sympathy particle at the end of a sentence. はやいね = "[that's] fast, isn't it?" It invites the listener to confirm.
〜よ — an assertion / new-information particle. はやいよ = "[I'm telling you] — [it's] fast!" Emphasizes something the listener doesn't yet know or isn't agreeing with.

V + ている — progressive / ongoing state. 走っている = "is running"; 見ている = "is looking"; 遊んでいる = "is playing." The て-form of a verb + いる. Formally this is step 12 (foregrounded in ch18) but it appears here naturally because the chapter is about ongoing action.
こと is the abstract "thing / fact" — often nominalizes adjectives or situations. いいこと = "a good thing"; そんなことはない = "that's not so."

かくれんぼ is built from ch05's かくれる — the word for the game grows out of the verb the reader already owns. 鬼 (おに) is the seeker's role-name in the game: ぼくが鬼だから、みんな、かくれて！ (The same word later names bigger, stranger things — remember it.)
遊ばない？ — a negative-form invitation, "won't you play?" Softer than a command; the everyday way children invite each other.
